text:
Tropic, why did you give me

hands full of color.

Everything I touch

will fill with sun.

On subtle afternoons in other lands

I will pass with my noises of iridescent glass.

Let me for a single instant

stop being cry and color.

Let me for a single instant

change the climate of my heart,

drink the half-light of a deserted thing,

lean in silence over a distant balcony,

sink into the mantle of fine folds,

scatter myself on the shore of a gentle devotion,

gently caress the straight hair

and write my meditation with a very fine pencil.

Oh, to stop being for a single instant

the Sun's Aide-de-Camp!

Tropic, why did you give me

hands full of color!

translation.title: Tropic, Why Did You Give Me...
translation.editorial_note: This first-line-title variant keeps the same poem with the source's capitalized final office of the Sun.
